method: Images downloaded via curl -L -A Mozilla/5.0 to scratch dir, viewed directly, deleted after. Videos not downloaded; classified from videos.json + existing viewed frames + no-transcript notes. Frames viewed directly from 03_images/video_frames/borth-coastal-defence-reef/ (excluding rejected/).

images.what_i_saw: Dredging/plant barge ('CAN LORO', tug 'AFON GOCH') loaded with white rock armour and a wheel loader, throwing up a large bow-wave. Rock armour material for the reef visible on deck, not yet placed.
Chain-link construction fence with red/white 'Construction Operations KEEP OUT' sign; Borth beach/seafront/houses behind; no reef or rock structure visible offshore.
Three excavators working along an offshore rock causeway/reef extending into calm sea, evening light.
Three Norton's-branded excavators plus a dump truck on a rock causeway/reef extending into calm water.
Komatsu excavator loading a dump truck on the same rock causeway/reef extending into the sea.

videos.evidence: videos.json what_it_shows: 'filming the coastal-defence/reef construction site at Borth in February 2011, early in the works'; silent, no captions/transcript
Frame AJXnUqQObJM_0015.jpg viewed directly: two excavators building the offshore rock reef, seen from the beach, matches title 'Borth sea defences and reef'
Frame QUB6s_F9dZc_0007.jpg viewed directly: houses, plant and a stockpile of rock/shingle on the seafront/onshore area, not the offshore reef structure itself
videos.json description: 'komatsu 450 separating rock and shingle', material sorting/grading for the works into 2012; not re-downloaded (embed_ok:false, no new media search performed)

frames.what_i_saw: Two excavators on an offshore rock spit/causeway, waves breaking on the sand in the foreground, overcast sky.
Borth seafront houses beside a shingle beach; excavators, dump trucks and a large stockpile of quarried rock/shingle in the foreground (onshore stockpile, not the offshore reef).

overall_verdict: No mislabelled or misleading media found in Borth's accepted image set. 4 of 5 images show the reef/causeway structure under active construction; the 1 remaining image is correctly limited in scope (construction-closure signage on the beach, no false reef claim). One frame (QUB6s_F9dZc_0007.jpg) is downgraded to site_context_only for precision (onshore stockpile, not the reef itself), but its existing caption was already accurate, not misleading. Unlike the beach-vs-reef mislabelling issue Lior flagged for other reefs, no image, frame or video here shows generic beach/surfing content mislabelled as reef content.
